pages.title: About HyperCom
pages.description:
HyperCom is an integrated information technology company founded by Dr Joshua A. Denila. We work with businesses of every size, from small enterprises to large corporations, on telecoms, internet technology and green energy.

EduSYS

EduSYS is our school management platform. A school's administration is the same work every term: admissions, fees, attendance, results, keeping parents informed. EduSYS puts that work in one place and automates what repeats, so that a school can give its attention to teaching.

Each school runs on its own web address, with its own data, staff and branding.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.description:
Last updated: 8 November 2026 · EduSYS, HyperCom

How HyperCom handles the information behind EduSYS: the school's account, the records a school keeps about its students, parents and staff, the payments made through it, and the messages it sends.

1. Who we are

EduSYS is a school management platform operated by HyperCom (“HyperCom”, “we”, “us”), a Nigerian information technology company with its head office at 14 Akinremi Street, Ikeja, Lagos.

HyperCom is the data controller for the information about schools that register with us and their owners and contacts, our billing records, and visitors to edusys.ng. For the records a school keeps in EduSYS about its students, parents, guardians, applicants and staff, the school is the data controller and HyperCom acts as a data processor on the school's instructions.

This policy covers the edusys.ng website, each school's EduSYS address (for example yourschool.edusys.ng), the EduSYS applications, and the email and SMS messages EduSYS sends. It does not cover websites or services we link to.

2. Information we collect

School and owner information

The school's name, address, web address and branding, and the name, email address and telephone number of the owner and the people who manage the school's subscription.

Records a school keeps

What a school chooses to record about its students and applicants: names, dates of birth, photographs, classes, guardians and their contact details, admission forms and documents, attendance, behaviour records, homework, examination marks, results and report cards, fees and payments, and library, transport and hostel records. About staff: names, contact details, roles, leave, attendance and payroll details.

Payment information

Subscription plan, number of students, invoices and payment status for schools; fee payments and admission form fees for parents and applicants. Card and bank details are entered with our payment providers (Paystack, Flutterwave, Monnify, Interswitch or Remita) and are not stored by EduSYS. For bank transfers we keep the receipt that is uploaded and the details entered with it.

Usage and technical data

Sign-in times, actions taken in EduSYS, IP address, browser and device type, and error logs. We use this to keep the platform secure and to help when something goes wrong.

Communications

Support requests, enquiries and quote requests, the files sent with them, and our replies.

3. How we use information

  • To provide the service: run each school's records, admissions, fees, results, messages and website as the school directs.
  • To administer accounts: set up schools and users, apply roles and permissions, and manage subscriptions.
  • To process payments: record subscription payments, fee payments and admission form fees, and confirm bank transfers.
  • To keep the platform secure: separate each school's data, detect misuse and investigate incidents.
  • To support schools: diagnose problems and correct records at the school's request.
  • To improve the service: understand which features are used and fix problems, using aggregated or de-identified data where possible.
  • To meet our obligations: keep accounting and tax records, and respond to lawful requests.
  • To communicate: service notices, security notifications and changes that affect a school.

4. Our legal bases

Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 we rely on the following bases, depending on the activity:

  • Performance of our contract with the school: operating EduSYS and providing support.
  • Legitimate interests: keeping the platform and its data secure, preventing misuse and improving the service, balanced against the rights of the people concerned.
  • Legal obligation: accounting, tax and responding to valid requests from regulators or courts.
  • Consent, where it is required, for example optional messages.

For the records a school keeps, the school decides its own lawful basis, as the controller.

5. Children's information

Many students are under 18. Their information is entered and controlled by their school, which is responsible for informing parents and guardians and for any consent the law requires. We process it only to provide EduSYS to that school, never for advertising, and we do not sell it or use it to build profiles.

6. Cookies

We use strictly necessary cookies to keep you signed in, protect your session and remember your choices, such as accepting cookies on a school website. These cannot be switched off without breaking the service. We do not use advertising cookies or sell data to advertising networks.

7. Who we share information with

We share personal data only as needed to run the service, and only with parties bound by confidentiality and data-protection obligations:

  • Hosting providers that store the platform and its data.
  • Email and SMS providers that deliver the messages a school or EduSYS sends.
  • Payment providers, for subscription payments, fee payments and admission form fees.
  • Video providers such as Zoom or Google Meet, where a school uses those add-ons.
  • Professional advisers, auditors and insurers, under confidentiality.
  • Authorities, where we are required by law or where disclosure is necessary to investigate misuse of the platform.
  • A successor entity, in the event of a merger, acquisition or transfer of the business.

A school's information is never visible to another school.

8. Where data is stored

EduSYS is hosted on cloud servers, and some providers may process data outside Nigeria. Where data leaves Nigeria we rely on contractual safeguards, access controls and the transfer conditions permitted by the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.

We do not sell personal data, and we never share a school's records with third parties for their own marketing.

9. How long we keep information

  • A school's records: for as long as the school's subscription is active. After it ends, we keep them for up to 90 days so the school can renew or ask for a copy, then delete them.
  • Records a school deletes: removed from the platform when the school deletes them, and from backups as the backups are replaced.
  • Billing and accounting records: for the period required by Nigerian tax and company law.
  • Support correspondence: normally up to 24 months after the request is closed.
  • Information that must be kept longer for a legal claim, or that we are required by law to retain, is kept only for that purpose.

10. How we protect information

Data is encrypted in transit. Each school's data is kept separate, and each user sees only what their role allows. Passwords are stored only as one-way hashes, and two-factor sign-in is available. Administrative access to the platform is limited to staff who need it.

No system is completely secure. If you believe an account has been compromised, contact the school, or us at info@hypercom.net.ng, immediately.

11. Your rights

Subject to applicable law, you may ask for access to your personal data, ask for it to be corrected or deleted, restrict or object to certain processing, ask for a portable copy, or withdraw consent you gave.

  • If you are a student, parent, guardian, applicant or member of staff, the school controls your records: please contact the school first. We will refer requests about a school's records to that school and help it respond.
  • Other requests can be sent to info@hypercom.net.ng. We verify identity before acting and respond within 30 days.
  • You may complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) if you believe your data has not been handled lawfully.

12. Responsibilities of schools

A school using EduSYS decides what it records and why. The school is responsible for having a lawful basis for its records, for informing students, parents, guardians and staff how their information is used, for setting roles and permissions appropriately, and for keeping its list of users current.

13. Changes to this policy

We review this policy as the service and the law change. The date at the top shows when it last changed. We tell schools about material changes before they take effect; using EduSYS after that date means the updated policy applies.

14. Contact us

Questions about privacy, or a request about your data, can be sent to info@hypercom.net.ng or +234 803 383 6341. HyperCom, 14 Akinremi Street, Ikeja, Lagos.

pages.title: Terms of Service
pages.description:
Last updated: 8 November 2026 · EduSYS, HyperCom

The agreement between your school and HyperCom for the use of EduSYS: what the platform does, what we are responsible for, and what we ask of you.

1. Agreement

These Terms of Service govern the use of EduSYS, a school management platform operated by HyperCom. By registering a school, accepting a quote, or using the platform, your school agrees to these terms. If you accept on behalf of a school or group of schools, you confirm you are authorised to bind it.

Where a signed agreement or an accepted quote sets different terms (for example price, term or support), that document takes precedence over these terms for that subject.

2. Definitions

  • “Platform”: the EduSYS web application, the school's EduSYS address and website, and related services.
  • “School”: the school or group that subscribes to the platform. “User”: a person the school gives access, such as staff, parents, guardians and students.
  • “School data”: the records and content the school and its users put into the platform.
  • “Subscription”: the paid right to use the platform for an agreed period and number of students.

3. The service

EduSYS lets a school manage admissions, student records, attendance, fees and payments, examinations and results, staff, messages and its own website, at its own web address.

The platform is a management tool. Its results depend on the information the school and its users enter. The school remains responsible for its own academic, financial and safeguarding decisions, and should check results, report cards and fee records before relying on them.

4. Accounts and access

  • Each school has its own workspace. The school's administrators create, disable and remove users, and decide what each user can see and do.
  • Sign-in details are personal. Users must keep them confidential and not share accounts.
  • The school is responsible for activity carried out under its users' accounts. Tell us immediately if you suspect unauthorised access.
  • We may suspend a user where we detect a security risk or misuse, and we will tell the school as soon as is practical.

5. Fees and payment

  • The subscription is charged per student, per term, at the rate for your school's size shown on our pricing page or in your quote. A one-time fee covers implementation and training.
  • You can pay each term or for the year. Payment is made online or by bank transfer before the period starts; a bank transfer is confirmed once we have checked the receipt.
  • If your number of students grows beyond what you paid for, you pay for the extra students at your current rate for the terms left in the period.
  • Fees exclude VAT and any similar charge, which are added where the law requires. SMS charges, payment gateway fees, video add-ons, custom work and hardware are not included.
  • We may change prices for future periods with at least 30 days' notice. A change does not apply to a period already paid.
  • If a subscription is not renewed when it ends, the school's access may be suspended until it is renewed. The school's data is kept as described in our Privacy Policy.

6. Acceptable use

You agree not to:

  • use the platform in a way that breaches Nigerian law or the rights of students, parents or staff;
  • resell, sublicense or provide the platform to another school or organisation without our written agreement;
  • reverse engineer, copy or scrape the platform, or try to get around its security, access controls or the separation between schools;
  • upload unlawful, harmful or infringing content, or use the platform to interfere with another school's service;
  • send messages through the platform that are unlawful, misleading or unsolicited.

7. School data and ownership

As between the parties, your school owns its school data. You grant HyperCom a limited licence to host, process, transmit, display and back up that data only to provide and support the service, to keep it secure, and to comply with the law.

We may use aggregated and de-identified information, which cannot identify your school, your students or your staff, to operate and improve the platform.

When a subscription ends you may ask for a copy of your school data. We keep it for the period set out in our Privacy Policy and then delete it.

8. Data protection

Each party complies with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and other applicable data-protection law. For the records the school keeps about its students, parents, guardians, applicants and staff, the school is the controller and HyperCom is the processor acting on the school's instructions. Our Privacy Policy describes what we collect and how we protect it.

The school is responsible for informing students, parents, guardians and staff about the information it keeps, and for any consent its own policies or the law require, in particular for students under 18.

9. Third-party services

The platform relies on third-party providers for hosting, email and SMS delivery, payment processing and optional video classes. Those services are subject to their own terms. We choose them carefully, but we are not responsible for outages, errors or changes on their side, and we will tell you when a provider issue affects your school.

10. Availability, maintenance and support

  • We work to keep EduSYS available at all times, apart from maintenance, which we schedule outside school hours where we can and announce in advance when it is planned.
  • Support is available by phone and email, Monday to Friday 9am to 4pm and Saturday 9am to 12pm.
  • We may change or withdraw individual features as the platform develops, and will give reasonable notice where a change materially affects your school.

11. Disclaimers

Except as stated in these terms, the platform is provided “as is” and “as available”. EduSYS does not replace the school's own checks on results, fees, attendance and safeguarding, and the school should verify important figures before acting on them.

12. Limitation of liability

To the extent permitted by Nigerian law, neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, loss of profit, business or goodwill, or for loss caused by events beyond its reasonable control.

Our total liability arising from or in connection with the service is limited to the fees your school paid for the service in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim.

Nothing in these terms excludes or limits liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, death or personal injury caused by negligence, or any liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

13. Indemnity

You indemnify HyperCom against third-party claims, losses and costs arising from your school's unlawful use of the platform, your breach of these terms, or content your school uploads that infringes another person's rights.

14. Intellectual property

The platform, its software, documentation, designs and marks are owned by HyperCom or its licensors. Your subscription grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the platform for your own school during the subscription; no other rights are granted.

If you send us suggestions or feedback, we may use them without obligation to you.

15. Confidentiality

Each party protects the other's confidential information with at least reasonable care, uses it only for the purposes of this agreement, and discloses it only to staff and advisers who need it. This does not apply to information that is public, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law.

16. Term, suspension and termination

  • The agreement runs for the subscription period and continues each time it is renewed.
  • Either party may end the agreement for a material breach that is not put right within 30 days of written notice.
  • We may suspend or end access immediately for unlawful use, or a security risk to the platform or other schools.
  • When the agreement ends, access ends, any outstanding fees become due, and school data is handled as described in section 7.

17. Changes to these terms

We may update these terms to reflect changes in the service or the law. The date at the top shows the current version. We tell schools about material changes at least 30 days before they take effect; using the platform after that date means you accept them.

18. Governing law and disputes

These terms are governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. The parties will first try to resolve any dispute in good faith within 30 days; if that fails, the dispute is referred to the courts of Lagos State, Nigeria.

19. Contact

Questions about these terms can be sent to info@hypercom.net.ng or +234 803 383 6341. HyperCom, 14 Akinremi Street, Ikeja, Lagos.
